claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires processing above 2300 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C has excellent mechanical properties.
Previous ZrB2 specimens manufactured at about 1700 °C were vulnerable to oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion.
Introducing 1–2 at% Si relative to the cation content will enable ZrB2 densification at approximately 1700 °C.
Si doping will form a thin in-situ SiOx intergranular film in ZrB2.
The Si-containing grain-boundary phase will produce liquid-phase-assisted sintering.
Si doping lowers the activation energy for ZrB2 densification by inducing a transient grain-boundary liquid phase.
The transient grain-boundary phase crystallizes or reorganizes into a stable protective silica layer during subsequent high-temperature exposure.
The silica layer retards oxygen ingress into ZrB2.
The silica layer retards penetration of molten plating metal into ZrB2.
The silica layer preserves the structural and mechanical integrity of Si-doped ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered at approximately 1700 °C will attain densification comparable to single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered at approximately 1700 °C will attain mechanical strength comparable to single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and previous lower-temperature specimens.
Si-doped ZrB2 will exhibit shallower liquid-metal corrosion penetration than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and previous lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed benefits apply around a 1700 °C processing temperature and at service temperatures up to approximately 1500 °C.
At very low Si concentrations, the protective silica layer may not form adequately.
At service conditions substantially beyond 1500 °C, the silica layer may become unstable and its benefits may be lost.
